Description
Whether you’re an investor looking for a solid and fine silver investment, or you’re looking for quality vintage
Silver Bars
to add to your collection, you will likely want to consider the Handy & Harman Vintage 100 oz Silver Bars .  Due to their long and complicated history, Handy & Harman Vintage silver products have always been held in high regard in the precious metals market.
Grab a piece of history at a very reasonable price. These don’t appear on the market that often, if at all.
Design of Handy & Harman Vintage 100 oz Silver Bars
Handy & Harman started in 1867 as Peter Hayden & Co in NYC, trading precious metals, then became Handy & Harman in 1886, refining and fabricating gold/silver alloys for jewelry and arts, later dominating the brazing alloy market by the 20th century. The company expanded significantly, diversifying into electronics, tubing (Handy-Tube), and other materials, but gradually divested its core precious metals refining in the late 90s, focusing on its broader industrial holdings, eventually becoming a diversified manufacturer under Steel Partners Holdings.
On the front side of the 100 oz Silver Bar you will see the weight and purity of the fine silver listed as well as the s name stamped on the plus a mysterious date code. Each one of these bars has a specific serial number associated with it so that it can be identified.
The back of these slabs is left blank. The majority of the 100 oz silver bars that are available on the market will be in moderate shape and will show signs of contact with other bars throughout their lengthy production period.
Please note that these Silver Bars 100 oz are no longer in production, the only ones available in the market are the circulated products and may show some form of wear and faded tones appropriate to their age.

Handy & Harman Vintage 100 oz Silver Bars
Contains 100 oz of .999 pure silver.
Silver Bars can either be hand-poured or machine-cut by Handy  & Harmen
Eligible for Precious Metal IRAs.
Features the Handy  & Harmen stamp, purity, and weight on the obverse side of the bar.
Refined by Handy  & Harmen
